en: Whenever restless, I would shoot mountain sheep,
Then turn back and lie at ease.
When the mighty hero lived,
I, poor wretch, would test my strength:
Setting them in rows, with my bow
I would shoot eighty in succession.
Such was my former nature,”
Said Külchoro, and thus
He spoke in verse of his former prowess
And the great conflicts,
And told of the mighty turmoil
That could never be healed.
Heroic Seytek heard his secrets
And readied himself like a hawk.
From the panther hero’s words,
Wisdom came to him from far away;
A sheathless sword was buckled on,
And your wretch blessed by the holy wanderer
Stepped forth, prepared to speak:
“My uncle Külchoro
Is the guardian above my head,
My fortune in heroic deeds.
From the traditions handed down,
And from questioning the wise,
I learned that assembled hosts stood together,
That he was an ember blazing like a minaret,
And throughout the whole wide world
There was none like my uncle.
He was a hero and a mainstay,
A lion surpassing all mankind.
He was one of those heroes
Who brought torment upon their foes in battle,
One of those souls who stirred
Great turmoil across the world.
His lashes were flame and his eyes embers;
No man was ever so fearsome!
When my uncle entered battle,
He burned forests into desert.
When he advanced, the enemy grieved;
His heroic, lionhearted prowess
Became known throughout the world.
The enemies who encountered him
Fell from their horses like severed sheaves.
When my uncle grew wrathful,
The people of the khagan fell.
He threw all who faced him into uproar,
And brought strife upon all he met.
He leveled even the soaring Ala-Too
With consummate skill;
He saved the Kyrgyz of Ala-Too from suffering
And made them a united people.
Building as he went, he made them homes;
Planting as he went, he made them orchards,
And guarded Talas as their homeland.
Among the peoples of the world, that noble soul
Made the renowned Choro a lion.
My uncle Semetey
Was perfect in every way;
If you looked within his heart,
It was broader than the face of the earth.
Such was my uncle,
Whose homeland was broad Talas,
Whose father was mighty, magnanimous Manas.
When I gathered together
The four corners of the earth,
When I subdued the whole wide world
And ruled it,
When I honed
The black-steel Zulpukor,
When I drove onward
All the peoples of the world,
Breaking ice to make a road
And bringing evildoers low,
Breaking rock to make a road
And bringing challengers low,
When I pursued all who fled
And let none escape,
When an enemy truly attacked,
If he grappled, I sent him on his final road
And dealt out punishment with my own hand.
No mortal dared face me;
No attacking enemy defeated me.
When I leveled my spear, it became flame;
When an enemy attacked, he ceased to exist.
He crossed the Urgench and opened a road;
He slaughtered heroic Kojo and brave Toltoy
And laid the two of them low.
He unleashed his fury fiercely
And slaughtered every warrior
Who boasted of his valor.
He broke through ravines and opened roads,
And laid hands upon the whole world.
A panther like a tiger,
My spearman uncle’s prowess
Was indeed beyond compare.
It was well known throughout the world
That his might was unsurpassed.
Plainly renowned and noble-browed,
His gray-maned valor stood apart.
Many called my tiger uncle Külchoro
A tiger among men,
Who devoured all he encountered.
When he tore men apart, he never had his fill of blood;
My uncle was a ravenous wolf.
My uncle, sustained by the sacred spirit,
Was called the people’s protector.
While strength remained across his broad back,
He made his gray-brown stallion dance;
Though countless myriads of foes came,
He hacked them down with his sword and subdued them,
Soaking his blade in blood.
Whoever provoked his wrath,
He killed and cast upon the ground.
Thick-armed and stone-hearted,
A full-limbed, bold young warrior,
He brought great calamity upon all he overtook.
He broke mountains and leveled the land.
Along the banks of Üch-Koshoy,
Where it meets the Talas,
On the flank lies Kan-Jailoo—
At the edge of Kan-Jailoo.
There is the dark gorge of Acha-Sai.
My son Seytek, listen well,
I have many a sorrow!
When the Argyn and Kyrgyz grew restless
And rode past in streaming ranks,
When strength, courage, and valor
Were being put to the test,
My elder Semetey
Would catch and slaughter a barren mare,
And among the broad-trousered, broad-chested,
Among the many broad-breasted men,
Among the comely champions,
He would test their strength.
Sixty barren mares and forty fillies
Would be staked as the prize.
A bull would be slaughtered,
And among the many men of steel,
The champions who entered battle,
Those skilled and ready with the spear,
The mighty men who knew the enemy’s wiles,
Those resourceful in counsel,
Who said, “Let my entrusted life be sacrificed,”
And offered up their lives,
Charging against the foe,
Guarding their people from the enemy—
My uncle would test them all.
From among the many stern-hearted men,
From champions whom the people tested,
From true gray wolves,
From those who stood beneath the banner,
From falcons who, for the common people,
Would sacrifice their lives,
My noble uncle Semetey
Would choose the finest.
When those consummately skilled with the spear,
Born superior to other men,
Across the whole wide world
Were raising a mighty tumult;
When the red Zulfikar sword
Was gripped and swung by its hilt,
Kicking through gorges and twisting them,
Felling every adversary,
Kicking ice and shattering it,
Striking down all who broke ranks,
And pressing ever onward;
When the whole wide world
Was held beneath our sway;
When our spirits surged at their height,
When we stood but a hair’s breadth from hell,
We would carve the haunch and feast,
And ask, “Where is any punishment?”
When Zulfikar hung
At our bare wrists;
When we subdued the whole world
And drove it before us;
When we bore away those who escaped
And kept them in our sights;
When the whole wide world
Was held beneath our sway;
When sprawling Kara-Shaar
Was held beneath our sway;
When we subdued those who grappled with us
And kept them in our sights;
When we shattered the front and left it bereft,
Subdued every enemy we met,
Shattered the flanks and left them bereft,
Subdued all whom we pursued,
And held them beneath our sway.
In the hollow of Jylgynduu,
Along the broad Talas,
In the palace with gates,
In the fortress of Üch-Koshoy,
At the dark eye of the spring,
Right beneath the plane tree,
On the flank lies Kötörmö,
In the hollow of Kötörmö,
Finding no host to challenge,
With my tufted spear and patterned sword
Brandished in my hand,
When I subdued the whole world
And lived in joy,
While my dear uncle was alive,
I would take up the mighty bow,
And this poor, grinning soul
Would put his strength to the test.
While my magnanimous uncle lived,
We plunged eagerly into every sport,
Testing our power and measuring our might,
Setting eighty mattocks upright,
And shooting an arrow through them.
While my mighty uncle lived,
We boisterous, valiant souls
Would test our strength.
Such was my former strength;
It was in the time of my uncle,
The leopard, gray wolf, and bloodthirsty lion.
When I held the wrathful khan of Beijing
At bay,
When I subdued the whole world
And set it ablaze;
When my trouser legs
Could scarcely contain my limbs,
When all the strength within my body
Could find no rest,
We shot through mattocks to test our strength,
Clashed together and fully tried our power.
Such was the nature
Of your once-vigorous uncle.
Unbroken and undivided,
He remained whole like this.
Such was the strength
Of your uncle who departed long ago:
For the prize, forty barren mares
Would be caught and slaughtered from the herd,
And we would test our strength.
Ninety barren mares would be slaughtered
For the swift and peerless champion,
The man who breathed more strongly than mortals,
Who, when chaos fell and enemies came,
When dust flew and the earth trembled,
When disaster befell a hero
And a hellish ordeal arrived,
Would go where none could survive,
Stake this precious life,
And grapple with the enemy.
From those who fought the fiercest,
Those consummately skilled with the spear,
The fortunate masters of stratagem,
Whose majestic forms seemed a myriad troops,
Whose eyes were round as hillocks,
Who seemed ready to devour any foe they saw,
Whose wrestling strength was unmatched,
Whose heroism was beyond measure,
From imposing warriors,
From broad-breasted champions,
